rules.title: General security deposit cap of one month's rent
rules.requirement: A landlord may not demand or receive security, however labeled, greater than one month's rent, in addition to first month's rent. Exceptions: small landlords who qualify (two-month cap), an advance payment of at least six months' rent on a lease of six months or longer, and fees the tenant agrees to pay for requested alterations.

rules.title: Small landlord security deposit cap of two months' rent
rules.requirement: A landlord who is a natural person, or an LLC whose members are all natural persons, and who owns no more than two residential rental properties with no more than four rental units in total may collect up to two months' rent as security. This higher cap does not apply when the prospective tenant is a service member, and the landlord may not refuse to rent to a service member because of this limit.

rules.title: Higher security charged to service members: disclosure and return
rules.requirement: If a landlord charges a service member a higher-than-standard security because of credit or housing history, the landlord must give a written statement of the amount and the reason. The extra amount must be returned after no more than six months if the tenant is not behind on rent, and the return date must be stated in the lease.

rules.title: Move-out and post-repair photographs of unit
rules.requirement: The landlord must photograph the unit within a reasonable time after it is returned and before any repairs or cleanings that will be deducted from the deposit. The landlord must also photograph the unit again after those repairs or cleanings are completed.

rules.quoted_span: (2) Beginning April 1, 2025, the landlord shall take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after the possession of the unit is returned to the landlord, but prior to any repairs or cleanings for which the landlord will make a deduction from or claim against the security deposit pursuant to this section, and shall also take photographs of the unit within a reasonable time after such repairs or cleanings are completed.

rules.title: Return of security deposit, itemized statement and permitted deductions
rules.requirement: Within 21 calendar days after the tenant moves out, the landlord must return the remaining security with an itemized statement. If the tenant paid electronically, the return must be electronic, and supporting documents and photos must be included when deductions exceed $125. Deductions are limited to reasonable amounts for unpaid rent, damage beyond ordinary wear and tear, cleaning, and restoring property; deposits cannot be called nonrefundable; and bad-faith retention can lead to damages of up to twice the deposit.

coverage.notes: Documentation requirements do not apply if deductions total $125 or less, or if the tenant signs a valid waiver, unless the tenant asks for documentation within 14 days. The initial inspection requirements do not apply to terminations under CCP § 1161(2)-(4).
